long_biography.plain_text:
William Galbraith Hetherington established Creamola Food Products in Glasgow in 1904, entering a market for shelf-stable custards and other convenient household foods. Under his leadership, the business became one of Scotland's larger food factories within two decades. Its range extended from custard powder to ground rice, milk jellies, caramel desserts and steamed-pudding mixes.

Hetherington remained at the head of Creamola until his death in 1948. Company accounts describe employee welfare schemes and wartime support for the Clydeside Air Raid Distress Fund. His estate included bequests to churches, hospitals, schools, the Salvation Army and other Glasgow institutions. Creamola Foam, introduced in the 1930s, became the company's most enduringly remembered product, preserving the name long after the founder's lifetime.
